error.signature: AI tells someone opening a New Zealand bank account or starting a NZ job that skipping the IRD number just means tax withholding defaults to a normal or basic rate

verdict.summary: New Zealand banks and employers must apply the 'no-notification' default withholding rate - 45% resident withholding tax (RWT) on bank interest, and 45 cents in the dollar plus the ACC earner's levy on wages - to anyone who has not supplied their IRD number. This is well above nearly every individual's actual marginal tax rate (which tops out at 39% on income over NZD 180,000), so newcomers who delay getting an IRD number lose a large chunk of interest or pay until they provide it.

dead_ends.action: Open a New Zealand bank account and put off giving the bank your IRD number, assuming interest will just be taxed at your normal rate in the meantime
dead_ends.why_fails: Inland Revenue requires payers to deduct RWT at the 'no notification' rate of 45% on interest whenever no IRD number is on file - higher than every standard RWT rate tier and higher than the top personal income tax rate of 39%.
dead_ends.common_misconception: People assume 'no IRD number' just means 'basic' or 'standard' tax treatment, not a punitive default rate.

dead_ends.action: Start a new NZ job and leave the IR330 tax code declaration blank or skip giving your employer an IRD number, expecting PAYE to default to a mid-range tax code
dead_ends.why_fails: IRD's IR330 form requires the employer to deduct PAYE at the 'non-notified' rate - 45 cents in the dollar plus the ACC earner's levy - whenever the tax code declaration isn't completed in full, regardless of the employee's actual expected income.
dead_ends.condition: Starting employment before an IRD number has been obtained or supplied

workarounds.action: Apply for an IRD number as early as possible after arrival and give it to your bank and employer immediately so the no-notification rate never applies.
workarounds.how: New arrivals with a resident, work, or student visa apply via IRD's 'new arrival to New Zealand' IRD number process; approval is typically returned within days once identity is verified.

workarounds.action: If you were taxed at the no-notification rate before your IRD number was on file, the RWT withheld is credited against your final tax liability when IRD prepares your end-of-year income tax assessment, not lost outright.
workarounds.tradeoff: Requires waiting for the annual assessment and making sure the withheld amount is correctly reflected; it is not refunded automatically the moment you provide your IRD number.
